To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FLC homologous genes exist outside the Brassicaceae and that they function in a manner similar to FLC in Arabidopsis.

1) we identified homologous sequences to Arabidopsis FLC in species from all three major angiosperm lineages, 2) the homologs from eudicots and monocots have similar gene structures and expression patterns, and 3) in sugar beet, BvFL1 is a repressor gene that is down-regulated by cold.

the sugar beet homolog of the Arabidopsis flowering time gene FLC is a floral repressor that is downregulated in sugar beet in response to vernalizing cold, suggesting that the FLC-mediated vernalization response has been conserved during eudicot evolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the vernalization pathway in plants.
the evolutionary conservation of the molecular mechanism underlying vernalization in the eudicots.
the evolution and molecular biology of flowering time control in the plant family Chenopodiaceae (which includes sugar beet and spinach).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FLC is the most conserved gene among flowering plants.
FLC homologues have been identified in the sugarbeet, and that the sugarbeet homologue, BvFL1, is a functional homologue of FLC in Arabidopsis and that it is downregulated in sugarbeet by cold.
the FLC-mediated vernalization pathway has been maintained throughout evolution of the eudicots, including the sugar beet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vernalization pathway is evolutionarily conserved across eudicot species, and that the vernalized state is a result of the downregulation of a floral repressor.
the vernalization mechanism is evolutionarily conserved among the angiosperms.
the vernalization mechanism in the sugar beet, a species that diverged from Arabidopsis more than 100 million years ago, is similar to that in Arabidopsis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vernalization pathway is conserved between dicot and monocot plants, despite the differences in the genes that are involved in the pathway.
vernalization is a conserved mechanism for the promotion of flowering in eudicots and that the molecular mechanisms underlying this response are likely to be highly conserved.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the vernalization mechanism in Arabidopsis have been conserved in sugar beet, and that these mechanisms may be conserved in many eudicot species.
